title: Free coherent monad modules and their augmented free resolution
statement:
Use the coherent-diagram, mapping-space and quasicategory conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the index categories and meaning of split augmented diagram of [lem-coef-infinity-split-augmentation-colimit]. Work in universes large enough for the following categories, with small mapping spaces in a possibly enlarged universe. Let $\mathcal C$ be an infinity-category. A coherent monad $T$ is a unital associative algebra in the monoidal infinity-category $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal C)$ under composition: it has unit $\eta:1\to T$, multiplication $\mu:T^2\to T$, and all associativity and unit compatibilities. Its module infinity-category $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Alg}_T(\mathcal C)$ consists of objects $A\in\mathcal C$ with action $a:TA\to A$ and all coherent unit and associativity data, retaining coherent module maps and their higher simplices. Let $V:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ forget the action. Then $V$ reflects equivalences and has a left adjoint $F$, with $VF=T$, free module $F(c)=(Tc,\mu_c)$, and natural equivalences
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(F(c),M)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,VM).$$
This equivalence sends a module map $f$ to $V(f)\eta_c$ and its inverse sends $g$ to the module map with underlying map $a_M T(g)$. These are coherent equivalences of mapping-space bifunctors, and the free adjunction unit is $\eta$.

For each $M=(A,a)\in\mathcal A$ there is a natural augmented coherent simplicial diagram $R_\bullet M\to M$ with $R_rM=F(T^rA)$ for $r\geq0$. For $r\geq1$, its underlying faces are
$$d_i=T^i(\mu_{T^{r-i-1}A})\quad(0\leq i<r),\qquad d_r=T^r(a),$$
and its underlying degeneracies are $s_i=T^{i+1}(\eta_{T^{r-i}A})$ for $0\leq i\leq r$. Its degree-zero augmentation has underlying map $a:TA\to A$. The augmentation $R_\bullet M\to M$ is colimiting in $\mathcal A$. The underlying augmented diagram $VR_\bullet M\to A$ extends coherently to $N(\Delta_{-\infty})^{\mathrm{op}}$; its extra degeneracies are $h_{-1}=\eta_A$ and $h_r=\eta_{T^{r+1}A}$ for $r\geq0$. All structures and their higher compatibilities are natural in $M$. Neither the existence of all geometric realizations in $\mathcal C$ nor preservation of arbitrary realizations by $T$ is assumed.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Corollaries 4.2.3.2 and 4.2.4.8, Construction 4.4.2.7, Example 4.7.2.7, Example 4.7.2.5 and Lemma 4.7.3.12; applied to the evaluation action of endofunctors on C. The free-module bar used in the proof of Lemma 4.7.3.13, printed pp. 688-689, is exactly this diagram. The colimit assertion is in the module category, and the splitting assertion is in C. Online source read; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact.

proof.text: Take $\mathcal V=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal C)$, with composition as tensor, acting on $\mathcal C$ by evaluation $H\otimes c=H(c)$. Tensor associativity here is composition of functors and the unit is the identity functor, so evaluation has its canonical coherent left-action structure. The given monad is the algebra $T$ in this monoidal category, and its coherent modules are exactly $\mathcal A$ in the statement. Apply [lem-coef-module-operadic-colimit-detection] to this action and $B=T$. Its equivalence clause says precisely that $V$ reflects equivalences; it requires neither colimits nor presentability.

source.place: Corollary 4.2.3.2, with the evaluation action of End(C).

proof.text: For $c\in\mathcal C$, construct $L_c$ as the object $Tc$ with action $\mu_c$; the algebra associativity and unit coherences of $T$, evaluated at $c$, give its full module structure. Put $\lambda_c=\eta_c$. The map in the hypothesis of [lem-coef-module-universal-arrow-criterion] is $\mu_c T(\eta_c):Tc\to Tc$, coherently homotopic to the identity by the right unit law. Hence composition with $\eta_c$ gives the required natural equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(L_c,M)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,VM)$. Apply the dual pointwise criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion] to $V$: these representing objects assemble to $F\dashv V$ and to equivalences of mapping-space bifunctors, with unit $\eta$. The actual construction $c\mapsto(Tc,\mu_c)$ and $g\mapsto T(g)$ is already coherent, since it evaluates the coherent multiplication of $T$; thus the representing functor may be identified with it and $VF=T$ with its specified coherence.

source.place: Definition 4.2.4.1 and Corollaries 4.2.4.6-4.2.4.8; assemble the universal arrows.

proof.text: For $g:c\to VM$, the map $a_M T(g):Tc\to VM$ is a coherent module map: its compatibility with the action is the chain $a_M T(g)\mu_c\simeq a_M\mu_{VM}T^2(g)\simeq a_M T(a_M)T^2(g)$; the two homotopies are naturality of $\mu$ and the coherent module associativity. More explicitly, write $\mu_c^{[k]}:T^{k+1}c\to Tc$ for the iterated free action and $a_M^{[k]}:T^kVM\to VM$ for the iterated module action, with the identity at $k=0$. For each $k$, the compatibility of $a_MT(g)$ with these actions compares $a_MT(g)\mu_c^{[k]}$ with $a_M^{[k]}T^k(a_MT(g))$. Naturality first moves $g$ to the last input; both composites then evaluate the $(k+1)$-fold action on $T^{k+1}(g)$. The higher comparisons are obtained by inserting this last-input map into the given coherent module operations. Restricting any parameter simplex restricts that input and those operations, so this construction specifies the coherent module-map data and a map of full mapping spaces. Under the equivalence from step 2 its image is $a_M T(g)\eta_c\simeq a_M\eta_{VM}g\simeq g$. Conversely, for a coherent module map $f:F(c)\to M$, the module-map homotopy gives $a_M T(V(f)\eta_c)\simeq V(f)\mu_c T\eta_c\simeq V(f)$. These are the unit and module-map coherences on whole mapping spaces, not merely equality of components. In particular this describes the homotopy inverse of the natural equivalence of step 2 and identifies the counit at $M$ with $a_M$.

source.place: Corollary 4.2.4.6; explicit inverse calculated from its defining universal-arrow map.

proof.text: Regard $T$ as a $(T,T)$-bimodule in End$(\mathcal C)$ using multiplication for both actions; their commuting coherences are the algebra associativity coherences. Apply [lem-coef-two-sided-coherent-bar-construction] with $P=T$ and $Q=M$. Its degree $r$ has underlying object $T^{r+1}A$, with left action $\mu_{T^r A}$, so it is $F(T^r A)$. The right action on $P$ gives $d_0=\mu_{T^{r-1}A}$, the interior contractions give $d_i=T^i(\mu_{T^{r-i-1}A})$, and the endpoint action gives $d_r=T^r(a)$. Unit insertion gives $s_i=T^{i+1}(\eta_{T^{r-i}A})$. The action pairing $T(A)\to A$ is $T$-linear and coherently balanced: both compatibilities are $a\mu_A\simeq aT(a)$ and its higher module coherences. The augmentation clause of that node therefore supplies a coherent cocone to $M$, with degree-zero map $a$. All of this takes place in $\mathcal A$, so the resulting faces and degeneracies are module maps and retain their higher coherences.

source.place: Construction 4.4.2.7; regular bimodule and action pairing, as in the bar in the proof of Lemma 4.7.3.13.

proof.text: Construct the splitting after forgetting the action by allowing a unit before the first $T$ factor. Explicitly this adjoins $h_{-1}=\eta_A$ and $h_r=\eta_{T^{r+1}A}$. Here is the ordered-word extension, including higher simplices. An object $\{-\infty\}\cup[n]$ is sent to the word consisting of $n+1$ copies of $T$ followed by $A$ (for $n=-1$ the word is just $A$). More precisely, identify the added least element with $-1$ for this formula. A map $f:\{-1,0,\ldots,m\}\to\{-1,0,\ldots,n\}$ with $f(-1)=-1$, read contravariantly, sends $T^{n+1}A$ to $T^{m+1}A$ as follows. The $j$th output $T$ factor, for $0\leq j\leq m$, uses the input factors with indices $f(j-1)+1,\ldots,f(j)$; contract a nonempty such block by iterated multiplication and use the unit for an empty block. The remaining factors $f(m)+1,\ldots,n$ act on $A$ by the iterated module action (for $m=-1$ all input factors act). This includes the case $f(j)=-1$, so initial output blocks can be empty. The map with $f(0)=-1$ and $f(j)=j-1$ for $j>0$ inserts exactly the new leading unit, giving the displayed $h_r$. This is the ordered-word evaluation of [lem-coef-two-sided-coherent-bar-construction] with the regular first factor also allowed to be the unit. The compatibility with unit blocks in that node makes this evaluation a coherent functor on $N(\Delta_{-\infty})^{\mathrm{op}}$; its restriction is the forgotten augmented bar of step 4. In low degrees $ah_{-1}\simeq1_A$ and $d_0h_r\simeq1$ are the module-unit and monad-unit coherences; $d_{i+1}h_r\simeq h_{r-1}d_i$ follows from naturality of $\eta$, and $s_{i+1}h_r\simeq h_{r+1}s_i$ follows from the same naturality, including $s_0h_r\simeq h_{r+1}h_r$. All higher compatibilities come from evaluating the same unit-block substitutions, rather than being inferred just from those pairwise identities. The extension is in $\mathcal C$; no assertion that the $h_r$ are module maps is used.

source.place: Example 4.7.2.7, the functor {−∞}*[n]*[0] and evaluation of the regular bar; Definitions 4.7.2.1-4.7.2.2.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-split-augmentation-colimit] the augmented diagram of step 5 is colimiting in $\mathcal C$. For every object $H$ of End$(\mathcal C)$, the same node says that applying $H$ to this particular cocone again gives a colimiting cocone. These are exactly the preservation hypotheses of [lem-coef-module-operadic-colimit-detection] for the evaluation action and the small index $N(\Delta)^{\mathrm{op}}$. Apply its arbitrary-cocone criterion to the actual module augmentation of step 4: its underlying cocone is colimiting, so the augmentation is colimiting in $\mathcal A$. This establishes the claimed realization even if no other realizations exist in $\mathcal C$ and even if $T$ preserves no arbitrary ones. Finally every operation used was evaluation of the monad, its unit/multiplication, or the action as a coherent functor of $M$; the bar node's naturality and the pointwise adjoint criterion retain all parameter simplices. Thus the augmentation, splitting and free-adjunction mapping equivalences are natural in the asserted coherent sense.

source.place: Example 4.7.2.5 and Corollary 4.2.3.5; Remark 4.7.2.4, and the regular module bar in Lemma 4.7.3.13.
